## Overview

LRPLF11 is the **level-factors** model for nonword reading (`nonword`).

_Off-floor likelihood + level-model crossover caveat._ Nonword reading is heavily floored, so the level outcome is the **off-floor indicator** (score $> 0$) at each timepoint, modelled by a Bernoulli; the linear predictor is the **log-odds of being off the floor at that timepoint** — pooling children who were never at floor, came off it, and returned to it — not a graded level. Under the revised DAG (`dag/dag-language-reading.dagitty`, revised 2026-07-10) measured skill parents are **deliberately excluded** as post-treatment mediators of the group×time effect; only the revised-DAG confounders speech (SP = `deapp_c`) and phonological memory (RW = `erbto`) — each with a missing-indicator — enter as adjusters. `group x time` is a per-timepoint off-floor log-odds gap for the group, parameterised as the adjusted t1 gap (`arm_gap_t1`, a pre-randomisation *balance* quantity, never an effect) plus the change in that gap at each later wave (`d_grp_time[t]`; #552); after t2 the waitlist crosses over, so the **clean randomised contrast lives only at t2** — the t2 change `d_grp_time[t2]`, a difference-in-differences of adjusted off-floor log-odds, labelled *causal*; the t3/t4 changes are post-crossover cohort/timing terms, and the per-wave gaps `b_grp_time[t] = arm_gap_t1 + d_grp_time[t]` are kept as a derived levels view. The child random intercept is only a partial, shrunken stand-in for between-child heterogeneity and does **not** control latent general ability. `ability x time` and `group x ability` complete the focal set. SES excluded (non-DAG / redundant).

## Model

$$
(N_t > 0) \sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(\operatorname{expit}(\eta_t)),\quad
\eta_t = \alpha + \alpha_{\text{time}[t]} + b_{\text{grp}[t]}\text{group}
  + \gamma_A A_{\text{std},t} + g_{\text{ability}[t]}z(\text{blocks})
  + \gamma_{\text{grp\_ability}}\,\text{group}\,z(\text{blocks}) + \sum_{c}\gamma_c\,z(c) + u_{\text{child}}.
$$

Here $\sum_{c}\gamma_c\,z(c)$ are the standardised speech and phonological-memory confounders (SP = `deapp_c`, RW = `erbto`), each with a missing-indicator; measured skill parents are excluded as post-treatment mediators. No `kappa` under the Bernoulli. Priors: shared template in `priors.py`.

![Model diagram](model_graph.png){#fig-model .lightbox fig-align="left"}

**Arm-gap parameterisation (#552).** The per-timepoint group coefficient is centred on the timepoint-1 arm gap: $b_{\text{grp}[t1]} = a_{t1}$ and $b_{\text{grp}[t]} = a_{t1} + d_{\text{grp}[t]}$ for $t \in \{t2, t3, t4\}$, where $a_{t1}$ (`arm_gap_t1`) is the covariate-adjusted immediate-minus-waitlist gap at t1 — before anyone was treated, so a **chance balance quantity** on the cross-coupling prior, reported and never read as an effect — and $d_{\text{grp}[t]}$ (`d_grp_time[t]`) is the change in that gap from t1, on the outcome-tier treatment prior. A levels model conditions on nothing at baseline while adjusting for age and ability at every wave, so a free per-timepoint vector (the pre-#552 parameterisation, retained as the `arm_gap_reference="free"` comparator) carries the covariate-adjusted chance t1 imbalance straight into the t2 contrast; centring on the t1 gap removes it and puts the prior on the randomised difference directly. The randomised contrast is therefore the **t2 change `d_grp_time[t2]`**, a difference-in-differences of adjusted levels; `d_grp_time[t3]` / `[t4]` are post-crossover associations, and the per-wave arm gaps `b_grp_time[t]` are kept as a derived levels view.

**Intercepts (#389 finding 2).** $\alpha$ is **anchored**: a pooled, arm-blind
empirical-Bayes anchor at the observed **pre-randomisation t1** logit plus a free
zero-centred offset, and $\alpha_{\text{time}}$ is an exact **zero-sum**
wave-deviation vector. The previous parameterisation — a free global intercept and
four free per-timepoint offsets, all centred at logit zero — was identified only
through its sums (posterior correlations to $-0.96$) and implied prior-predictive
scores near half the instrument maximum for a population observed far below it.
The anchor uses only pre-randomisation data, so no treatment-affected quantity
enters the prior; the priors table labels the offset as empirical Bayes.
